objective.statement: Tell flags from beams and know how many notes a beam joins.
successCriteria: I know a beam does the job of the flags when short notes are grouped.
I know one beam means quavers and two beams mean semiquavers.
I can work out how long a beamed group lasts.

explanation.text: A single quaver or semiquaver is written with flags on its stem. When several short notes sit together, their flags are joined into a straight line called a beam.

music.textAlternative: A single quaver with a flag, followed by two quavers joined by a beam.

explanation.caption: A flagged quaver on its own, and two quavers joined by one beam.

explanation.text: One flag, or one beam, means quavers. Two flags, or two beams, mean semiquavers. The beam tells you the value in exactly the same way as the flags.

music.textAlternative: Four semiquavers joined by two beams.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 4 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver).

explanation.caption: Four semiquavers joined by two beams: together they last one beat.

explanation.text: Beams make music easier to read because they show where the beats are. You will use them to group notes in the next unit.

music.textAlternative: A pair of quavers joined by one beam, then four semiquavers joined by two beams.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), 4 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver).

steps: Look at the first group: one beam, two notes. These are quavers, a half beat each.
Look at the second group: two beams, four notes. These are semiquavers, a quarter beat each.
Press Play all: both groups last one beat, though one has two notes and the other four.
demonstration.textAlternative: A beamed pair of quavers and a beamed group of four semiquavers, each lasting one beat.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.
mistakes.dot-misread: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.
mistakes.beam-count-off: Count the noteheads that are joined by the beam, one by one.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.

recap: Beams join the flags of short notes that sit together.
One flag or beam = quaver; two flags or beams = semiquaver.
A beamed group is counted note by note, just like separate notes.
